clusters.name: Starting secondary school and family shifts, 1987
clusters.reason: Around the time Jonah began secondary school, his distance from his stepfather deepened while his tie to his father strengthened. His stepparents' marriage fractured over whether to have a child, and Jonah's anxiety rose as he made the chess squad but felt out of his depth.

clusters.name: Grandfather's death and unravelling at conservatory, 1989–1992
clusters.reason: Jonah's grandfather died in June 1991 after years of illness. Within months, Jonah injured his wrist and stopped playing, lost his closest friendship with Rafe, and sank into isolation and low functioning. His mother had remarried in autumn 1992. Around the same time, his grandfather Gordon died. Through this stretch Jonah's anxiety, symptoms and underfunctioning mounted: he was getting high, absorbed in radios, lost and unable to get going. His functioning collapsed.
clusters.change: Your grandfather Gordon died in June 1991 while you were at the conservatory. Around the same time your mother remarried. The picture shows a year when several things shifted at once—your grandfather gone, your music stopped, your friendship broken, your mother's remarriage underway—and you lost your way.

clusters.name: Relationship ending and insomnia, 1998–1999
clusters.reason: Jonah bonded with Joelle in early 1998. By 1999 his insomnia worsened before performances, though he was playing the best he ever had and winning competitions. Within months they separated. He began therapy with Victor Halloran after the split, reading about families with gamblers and asking what that meant for him.

clusters.name: Burnout, grandmother's death, and depression, 2001–2004
clusters.reason: In autumn 2001 Jonah began running out of steam for performing. Around the same time his grandmother Winifred was found to have bowel cancer and underwent operations and chemotherapy. In early 2002 Jonah had a disastrous audition and began casting about. He withdrew from family and left Thornbury for Gull Harbour. He met Marisol and moved to Fenwick with her, but they split within the year. He returned to Thornbury and sank into deep depression, hardly moving from the sofa. He could not face his family. His grandmother died in February 2004. Over those years—his burnout, her illness and death, his failed audition, his distance from his family—Jonah's functioning collapsed and his symptoms mounted. He began swimming to help sleep, asked his parents for help with therapy costs, and returned to Victor Halloran. As his grandmother declined he visited her briefly, hung over, on the way to the airport, and regrets cutting the visit short.

Across those years your functioning fell, your symptoms rose, and you pulled back from your parents and nearly everyone else. The stretch from autumn 2001 through the winter after her death was when the bottom fell out.

clusters.name: Grandmother's death and cutoff from mother, 2008
clusters.reason: In January 2008 Jonah's maternal grandmother Lorna died, and his grandfather Clifford died around the same time. Four weeks before nursing school, Jonah was building at Alder Creek with Silas when his mother pressed to visit him against his wishes. The visit went wrong and she never got inside. He kept the door shut on her. When he left for nursing school in Marlow Sound, he stopped speaking to his mother—a silence that held for roughly a year. Within months, his aunt Imogen had a stroke. His sister's partner Bree had a child. The events show distance piling up: Jonah too drained to speak with his mother, her pushing past his wishes, conflict between them, then his cutoff.

clusters.name: Marriage to Wren and family strain, 2017–2019
clusters.reason: Jonah married Wren in March 2017. After the wedding he saw his mother somewhat less. Around the same time his cousin Alice was diagnosed with multiple sclerosis. His sister Tara married and had a baby. His aunt Imogen's condition worsened—she lashes out when muddled. Leo and his family returned to live nearby. In October 2019, around Wren's family's retirement celebration at the lake, Jonah's sleep collapsed entirely—awake from the small hours and unable to sleep. He felt he didn't belong among her family. Wren was swamped by events and he overfunctioned laying out a plan to settle her. She and her father and brother are tightly fused, talking all day. Jonah carries constant anxiety about driving projects forward. The picture shows a year when his married life with Wren deepened his contact with her family's anxiety and fusion while his contact with his own family eased off, and his sleep fell apart around her family gatherings.
